text: Zero comes from an Arabic word... and so does the word for a secret code.
Sifr. It means empty. When Indian numbers reached Baghdad, the sign for nothing was called sifr.
In 1202, Fibonacci took it to Italy as zephirum... it shrank to zefiro... and then, zero.
But sifr took a second road: cifra... then cipher. First it meant zero... then any number... then a secret code.
Your turn. The same three letters are in al-Baqarah, about a cow. Empty, zero, or yellow?
YELLOW! A bright yellow cow. Same letters... a different word.
So what's your favourite number? Comment it... and zero doesn't count!
